package.title: 100 Pakistan Geography and Map Skills MCQs with Explanations

questions.question: Which sea lies along Pakistan’s southern coastline?
Which country lies to the west of Pakistan?
Which country is situated northeast of Pakistan?
Which country lies mainly east of Pakistan?
Which Pakistani province has a coastline on the Arabian Sea?
Which listed region is landlocked and mountainous in Pakistan’s far north?
The Potohar Plateau is located mainly in which province?
The Thar Desert is primarily associated with which Pakistani province?
The Cholistan Desert is in which province?
The Kharan Desert is associated with which province?
Which river is the principal river of Pakistan’s Indus Basin?
Which river flows through the city of Lahore?
Which river flows through the valley of Kashmir before entering Pakistan-administered territory?
Which river flows through Peshawar before joining the Indus?
Which river is associated with the city of Multan and joins the Indus near it?
Which river joins the Chenab at Trimmu in Punjab?
Which river is the easternmost of the five major Punjab rivers named in the traditional Punjab grouping?
Which river is the westernmost of the five rivers in the traditional Punjab grouping?
Where does the Indus River ultimately discharge?
In which general direction does the Indus flow through most of Pakistan?
K2 belongs to which mountain range?
Nanga Parbat is part of which mountain system?
Tirich Mir is the highest peak of which range?
Which range lies along much of the border between Balochistan and Sindh?
The Salt Range is located mainly in which province?
Which plateau is located in northern Balochistan around Quetta and adjoining areas?
The Deosai Plateau is in which northern region of Pakistan?
Which broad plain is formed largely by deposits from the Indus and its tributaries?
Which landform best describes the Makran region along Pakistan’s southwestern coast?
Which pass connects the Peshawar region with Afghanistan through the border mountains?
Which pass connects Pakistan with China in the Karakoram region?
Which pass provides a route between the Quetta area and the plains near Sibi?
Which pass is associated with the route between Dir and Chitral?
Which pass lies on a traditional route between Afghanistan and Pakistan through South Waziristan?
Which is the correct order of the four principal compass directions clockwise from north?
A traveller faces east and turns right. Which direction does the traveller face now?
A vehicle is heading south and makes a left turn. Which direction is it heading afterward?
A hiker walks north, then turns 90 degrees clockwise. What direction is the hiker facing?
What bearing, measured clockwise from north, represents due east?
What bearing represents due south when measured clockwise from north?
A map bearing is 270°. Which cardinal direction does it indicate?
A person walks 4 km north and then 4 km south along the same straight route. Where are they relative to the starting point?
A person walks 3 km east and then 4 km north. What is the straight-line distance from the start?
From a starting point, a traveller goes 6 km north and 8 km east. What is the shortest distance back to the start?
A town lies northeast of a village. In which direction is the village from the town?
On a standard map with north at the top, what direction is to the left?
On a map, a location is at 32° N, 74° E. What does 32° N describe?
What does the coordinate 70° E describe?
choices: Longitude east of the Prime Meridian
Longitude west of the Prime Meridian

questions.question: Which line of latitude is defined as 0°?
Which reference line is defined as 0° longitude?
Which coordinate changes when moving directly north or south along a meridian?
Which coordinate changes when travelling directly east or west along a parallel of latitude?
A map scale states 1 cm represents 2 km. What ground distance does 6 cm represent?
At a scale of 1 cm to 5 km, what distance on the ground is represented by 3 cm?
A map uses the scale 1:100,000. What ground distance does 1 cm represent?
On a 1:50,000 map, two points are 4 cm apart. What is their ground distance?
A road is 18 km long. On a map with a scale of 1 cm to 3 km, how long is the road on the map?
On a map with a scale of 1:25,000, how far on the ground does 2 cm represent?
A map scale is 1 cm to 4 km. A route measures 7.5 cm. What is its ground length?
A 24 km route is shown as 6 cm on a map. What ground distance does 1 cm represent?
A map scale of 1:200,000 is used. What ground distance does 3 cm represent?
On a map, 1 cm represents 8 km. How many centimetres represent 40 km?
A straight line measures 2.5 cm on a 1:40,000 map. What is the ground distance?
A map scale is 1:250,000. What distance on the map represents 5 km on the ground?
A map shows a river segment as 9 cm. The scale is 1 cm to 2 km. What is the segment’s ground length?
A map’s scale is 1:500,000. What does 1 mm on the map represent on the ground?
A route of 15 km is represented by 5 cm. What is the scale in words?
Which statement correctly describes a large-scale map compared with a small-scale map of the same area?
choices: It shows more detail over a smaller area
It shows less detail over a smaller area
It shows more area with more detail
It always uses a smaller paper sheet

questions.question: Which type of map is most useful for showing the heights and shapes of land?
On a contour map, what does a contour line connect?
On a contour map, what do tightly spaced contour lines generally indicate?
On a contour map, what do widely spaced contour lines usually indicate?
If a map has no north arrow but its grid is aligned with the page edges, what direction is conventionally at the top?
Which direction is opposite southeast?
A traveller faces west and turns left. Which direction does the traveller face?
A boat travels on a bearing of 045°. Which direction is closest to this bearing?
A plane flies on a bearing of 135°. Which direction is closest to its course?
A person walks 5 km west and then 5 km east. What is the net displacement?
A hiker walks 2 km south, then 2 km east. In which general direction is the hiker from the starting point?
Town B is due west of Town A. In which direction is Town A from Town B?
Which pair of directions are opposite on a compass?
In which general direction is the Indus Delta from the city of Lahore?
In which broad direction is the Karakoram region from Karachi?
Which option correctly identifies Pakistan’s broad climate contrast?
choices: Arid conditions dominate much of the country, while northern high mountains are markedly cooler
The entire country has a uniform equatorial climate
The whole country is covered by permanent ice

questions.question: Why is the Indus Plain generally more suitable for extensive farming than the high Karakoram?
choices: It has broad, low-lying alluvial land and river irrigation
It is higher and colder than the Karakoram
It is a permanent ice sheet

questions.question: Which region is most directly associated with glaciers and very high mountain peaks?
Which feature is most likely to be found where a large river meets the sea and deposits sediment?
What is a watershed divide?
choices: A channel where two rivers merge
A flat area at a river mouth
A line joining equal elevations only

questions.question: A tributary is best described as what?
choices: A smaller river that flows into a larger river
A river mouth formed by sediment
A canal that always flows into the sea

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes a plateau from a plain?
choices: A plateau is elevated relatively flat land; a plain is broad low-relief land
A plateau is always below sea level; a plain is always mountainous
A plateau is a river mouth; a plain is a pass
They are both names for a glacier

questions.question: Which description best fits a mountain pass?
choices: A lower route through a mountain barrier
A flat area at a river mouth
A dry basin with no outlet

questions.question: On a map with a north arrow, a river flows from a point at 33° N to one at 30° N. In which general direction has it moved?
A location at 68° E is compared with one at 72° E on the same parallel. Which location is farther east?
choices: Latitude determines which is farther east

questions.question: A location at 35° N is compared with one at 30° N on the same meridian. Which is farther north?
choices: Longitude determines which is farther north

questions.question: A map uses 1 cm to represent 10 km. A measured route is 0.8 cm. What is the ground distance?
On a 1:100,000 map, what map distance represents a ground distance of 3 km?
A map shows a route as 12 cm at a scale of 1 cm to 1.5 km. What is the ground distance?
A 1:20,000 map shows two points 7 cm apart. What is the ground distance in metres?
A route covers 36 km and appears as 9 cm on a map. What is the scale in kilometres per centimetre?
A 1:300,000 map shows a distance of 2 cm. What is the ground distance?
